column1: # local-ci stage budget (#1551, re-derived for #1562/#1568, conditioned per stage for #1604).
# A ceiling is measured, never estimated, and it is measured **in the condition it is enforced in**.
# There are two conditions, because a subject that compiled crates and one that compiled nothing are
# not the same experiment — and the subject of every row's ceiling is that row (a stage, or the run):
#   warm — the stage compiled **nothing**: this is the column that describes a stage doing its work on
#          a tree that is already built
#   cold — the stage compiled **at least one crate**: it paid a compile inside its own wave, and the
#          other seven stages of the same run may be warm. One crate is a yes; the threshold is 1, not
#          COLD_CRATES, because on a stage the question is "did this stage pay a compile?"
# `total` is the one row whose subject is the **whole run** — and it answers the same question by the
# same rule: 0 crates built is the nothing-built column, one or more is the built-something column.
# There is no run-level crate threshold. There used to be (`COLD_CRATES = 100`), and it made a 31-crate
# run "warm": judged against a 12m50s ceiling sampled from runs that built nothing, while the run itself
# took 23m10s because the compile is real and is charged to the run (#1612). One crate is a yes.
# #1604 is why the two are separate. `0976e62f` was a warm run (19 crates, cold at 100+) in which
# `lint` built all 19 of them and took 8m25s — judged against a 1m48s ceiling sampled from four runs
# whose `lint` built nothing. The run was warm; the experiment was not. One regime for the run applied
# one column to every stage, and stages are exactly what differ.
# "Compiled" is counted from cargo's own machine stream — `cargo <subcommand>: N crate(s) built`, printed
# by the language wrapper from the `compiler-artifact` messages that are not fresh, deduplicated by
# package. A stage where no step printed such a line is **unmeasured**, and it is judged on the cold
# column: judging it warm would be calling an unmeasured stage cheap (see #1599, where a masked wrapper
# made an eleven-minute stage count zero crates and the warm ceilings were applied to a cold run).
# "Ran no cargo" is not that. `docs` and `integration` invoke no cargo at all — the stage did its work
# and built nothing, and there was nothing to measure — so they are nothing-built, on the warm column.
# The distinction is the **runner's own record**, not a reading of prose: a step that invokes cargo
# writes `cargo-step: <label>` into its stage transcript, so "this stage ran cargo" is a fact the tool
# recorded rather than a word that happened to appear (#1606 — the previous version grepped the
# transcript for `cargo <word>` and called `guards` unmeasured because a guard printed "cargo
# wrapper(s)"). A recorded step with no count line is the blind case and takes the cold column.
# `coverage` is recorded but not counted: its `cargo llvm-cov` runs inside `coverage.sh`, which owns its
# own invocation, and `cargo llvm-cov` has no `--message-format`. The stage therefore stays `unmeasured`
# — the honest answer — until that script reports; the marker is the runner saying "there is cargo work
# here I cannot see", which is different from silence and different from a count.
# Columns, per stage: the ceiling in each condition, the sample it was derived from — `runs` (how many
# measured runs) and `slowest` (the slowest of them) — and `compiled`, the crate count those runs'
# stages reported. `compiled` is what the ceiling is conditioned on, so a ceiling cannot be read without
# knowing the experiment that produced it. `unmeasured` is a value: it says the sample was taken before
# the counter could see what it was counting (#1599), and the next re-baseline replaces it with a number.
# A numeric `compiled` cell is checked for consistency with its column by
# `.pi/scripts/validate-budget-derivation.sh`: a warm stage sample must have compiled 0, a cold one at
# least 1, and `total`'s warm sample fewer than COLD_CRATES — a warm sample whose runs compiled crates
# is refused, because it is a measurement of a different experiment under this column's name.
# Derivation, applied by `.pi/scripts/validate-budget-derivation.sh` to every cell:
#   ceiling = floor(11 * slowest / 10)     integer arithmetic: (slowest*11) / 10
#   cold    = max(floor(11 * cold_slowest / 10), warm ceiling)
# The same rule for both columns of a stage, applied to the sample each column was measured from — one
# shape to check rather than two.
# The **band** is the movement this table treats as noise, per row, in integer seconds:
#   band = min(78, warm_ceiling)        for a stage;   band = 0 for `total`
#   78   = 1.3 min x 60 = 13 x 6        the largest per-stage run-to-run spread recorded in
#                                       `.github/ci-budgets.tsv` (0.4-1.3 minutes per stage)
# A row that overshoots its ceiling by no more than its band **warns** and does not fail; beyond it,
# it fails. This is the CI-side gate's rule (`ci_budget_report.sh`, FAIL_OVERAGE 1.5 min, #1523)
# applied to the local numbers: failing inside a band the project has already measured teaches people
# to raise ceilings until the failures stop, which is how a budget becomes a comment. The cap at
# `warm_ceiling` keeps a short row honest — a 1-second stage cannot be 78 seconds of noise, because
# that is twice its whole budget.
# `total` has no band: its subject is the run, and a run that overshoots by four minutes is not the
# same code measured twice. `validate-budget-derivation.sh` recomputes every band from these two
# rules and from the spread recorded in `.github/ci-budgets.tsv`.
# The conditioning rule the guard also checks:
#   a warm stage sample compiled nothing; a cold stage sample compiled at least one
# Integer arithmetic on purpose: (700*11)/10 = 770, where `ceil(1.10 * 700)` in floating point is 771,
# because 700*1.1 is 770.0000000000001. The earlier table was written by three different expressions —
# `ceil` for four cells, Python's banker's `round` for the rest, and a hand edit for one — so seven of
# its eighteen cells were not the number its header stated (#1582). A rule a reader can re-derive in a
# shell is a rule the file can be checked against, and `.pi/scripts/validate-budget-derivation.sh` is
# that check: it recomputes every cell and exits 1 on a one-second disagreement.
# Floor rather than ceil because the margin is a margin, not a target: 10% below a measured run is
# already more room than the run used, and every recorded run still fits inside the result — the
# slowest warm `lint` (99s) is under 108, the slowest cold `guards` (201s) under 221. A ceiling that
# rounds up is a ceiling that grows a second per derivation.
# `coverage` cold deserves the note that #1582 asked for: it read 381, one second *above* both rules,
# because the pass that added the sixth cold run wrote `max(..., warm_ceiling + 1)` — the
# "never below the warm one" rule implemented as strictly above. It is now 380, equal to the warm
# ceiling and derived, because in a cold run `coverage` is the *second* stage to pay for the same
# compile: 345s slowest in both regimes is a measurement, not a mistake.
# The samples are full runs (`local-ci.sh`, stages in their own waves), never `--stage <name>`: a stage
# measured alone is a different experiment — #1551 measured `guards` at 2m13s alone and 43s in a run.
# Every sample cell below records `unmeasured` for `compiled`, and that is a fact, not a gap: the warm
# sample was four full runs and the cold sample six, all taken while the stage counters could not see
# what they were counting (#1599's masked stderr). The durations are honest; the compile counts of
# those runs were never recorded, so the conditioning cannot be certified for them and the file says so
# instead of writing a zero it did not measure. The re-baseline that follows #1604 replaces these cells
# with numbers from runs taken under the corrected counter, and `validate-budget-derivation.sh` will then
# refuse a warm cell that is not 0.
# Warm sample: four full runs on 2026-11-15 at build times 7-16s (8m13s, 8m28s, 9m33s, 7m47s wall
# clock). The `total` row has a fifth: the owner's 11m40s run, 700s, one second over the old 699s
# ceiling — the datum that made the old ceiling's provenance worth asking about.
# The cold ceiling is never below the warm one — a cold run cannot be bounded tighter than a warm run
# of the same stage — and equality is allowed: `coverage` is the case, for the reason above.
# Cold sample: six full runs on the same date at build times 64-688s (13m06s, 15m26s, 19m30s,
# 36m28s, 36m30s, and 27m12s after `cargo clean`, which compiled 488 crates). Two of them are the
# 36-minute rebuilds that the old single-column ceiling called regressions. The 27m12s run is also
# what fixed `guards`: on a cold tree it compiled 38 crates inside its wave and took 3m21s, against
# 2m10s cold in the earlier sample — the cold column absorbs a compile that lands in a stage's wave,
# which is exactly what one ceiling could not do.
# `total` bounds the run, not a stage: eight stages each inside their ceiling can still be a run
# nobody would accept.
# A ceiling is raised with a measurement, the date and the machine. A ceiling nudged to fit the last
# run is a comment that fails the person next week.
